For “Roth GraphER reranking RAG”, the closest match is GraphER, which proposes a graph-based enrichment and reranking framework for retrieval-augmented generation. It builds a query-time graph using proximity relationships beyond semantic similarity, then applies graph-based ranking to surface top candidate documents, with experiments showing improvements in retrieval completeness across table retrieval, multi-hop retrieval, and long-document retrieval, and noting no additional graph infrastructure and retriever-agnostic integration with standard vector stores. [1]

If instead you meant listwise reranking without explicit graphs, L2G induces an implicit document graph from listwise reranker logs and enables scalable graph-based retrieval without explicit graph computation or additional LLM calls. [2] If you meant rerankers aligned to downstream generation quality, RRPO uses reinforcement learning with LLM feedback to optimize reranking for context utility. [3]

None of the provided papers mention “Roth” specifically, so the results only partially address the request via GraphER-related reranking for RAG. [1]
